The agent's own mechanism says 'Overlaps with P_RAILWAY_CAPEX (De-duplicate: use the railway edge for rail-specific changes)', but both edges are live and EV_BUDGET27_CAPEX_RAILWAY hits both (+1.08 and +0.86 expected). Keep 0.3 for non-rail infra lending, which P_INFRA_SPENDING_ROADS partly covers already.

Double count. The mechanism (deficit monsoon -> cooling demand and lower hydro -> higher thermal PLF) is exactly the backbone F_MONSOON -> F_POWER_DEMAND_IN (-0.72) and F_MONSOON -> F_POWER_PRICE_IN (-0.38) edges. ADANIPOWER has direct edges to both, and the power-price recent state is the observed IEX change (director override 1.9). The direct edge books +3.1% since June on top of +4.4% (price) and +1.9% (demand), plus -2.1% and -1.2% forward from monsoon events. Keep 0.25 for the residual hydro-substitution PLF effect.

The agent calls the sign 'ambiguous': fewer rain days help construction, but a deficit monsoon hurts rural housing and IHB demand. Since June it books +1.25% 'unpriced' upside from the driest monsoon since 2015, while Ambuja itself flagged a demand slowdown (Reuters 28 Jul 2026; Q1 revenue -8%, Q2 PAT -90% on 29 Oct). Remove it rather than keep a coin-flip sign.

The node's only occurred shock is EV_EXPORT_LEVY_REVISIONS (diesel Rs11.5/l, ATF levy, 31 Oct), which books -4.0% on Hindustan Zinc since June although no metals levy exists. The real tail risk, a windfall levy on zinc/silver, should be a HINDZINC company event (see findings). This changes HINDZINC since-June from -11.4 to about -7.4 beta-adjusted, still below the realised -14.0, so unpriced stays 0.

EV_BUDGET27_CAPEX_RAILWAY.reason: Level-versus-surprise error. The description says 'Base case: central capex growth ~10% ... (model assumption; no fetched figures)', yet F_GOVT_CAPEX +0.8 SSU is booked at p=0.9, so the expected outcome counts as a +8pp positive surprise that is only half priced. Fiscal evidence points the other way. H1 FY27 capex grew 12% (BusinessLine, 30 Oct 2026) after 18% in Apr-Aug, so it is decelerating. The H1 fiscal deficit is 42.1% of BE, a five-year high (FE/Livemint, 30 Oct 2026), and an ET report (2 Oct 2026) sees H2 growth slowing 'as capex moderates'. The catalogue's own EV_BUDGET_FY28_FISCAL_SLIPPAGE is at p=0.5. This event is the largest forward item for SIEMENS (+3.4 incl. rail), TMCV (+2.9), PNB/UNIONBANK (+2.4), CUMMINSIND (+2.0), IRFC (+1.9) and AMBUJACEM (+1.5). Sources: https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=central+government+capex+April-September+CGA+when:40d&hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN:en

recent_state_overrides.reason: The event sum of 1.5 is made of ALMM List-II +0.5 and the BESS VGF +1.0. (1) ALMM-II's 1 Jun 2026 effective date was notified by MNRE in Dec 2024 (model knowledge), so the change since 1 Jun is nil. It also raises developer capex (FE, 21 Aug: 'solar project costs may rise 20%'), which is negative for IPPs (AGEL, Tata Power RE), not 'stronger support'. (2) The BESS VGF is confirmed (PIB/PM India, The Hindu, Moneycontrol, 4 Nov 2026: Rs14,500 cr for 92 GWh). It is a capex grant that competitive tariffs pass to discoms. At +1.0 SSU it books about +6% on AGEL (~Rs14,000 cr of market cap, roughly the whole subsidy) plus +4% on Tata Power and +4.8% on AESL. (3) PM-DHARA (Rs1.86 lakh cr green-energy transmission, Cabinet 30 Sep 2026) is missing from the catalogue, but power stocks fell on the day ('Power stocks fall despite PM-DHARA', Livemint 1 Oct), so the market's sensitivity to such announcements is low. Net change since June: BESS VGF ~0.3 + PM-DHARA ~0.3 = 0.6. This cuts unpriced since-June impact by about 5.4pp on ADANIGREEN, 3.6pp on TATAPOWER and 4.3pp on ADANIENSOL, the largest single item in all three.

The only occurred shock is EV_BESS_VGF_NOV26 (+0.5), which also shocks P_RENEWABLE_SUPPORT +1.0, so one Rs14,500 cr scheme is counted on two theme nodes (AGEL 6+2 = +8%, Tata Power 4+1.5). Scale it in line with the P_RENEWABLE_SUPPORT reassessment above.

The state of +1.0 comes from EV_GDP_Q1FY27_7_8's note 'capex +18% Apr-Aug'. Updated CGA data show capex +12% in April-September (BusinessLine, 30 Oct 2026), close to the ~10% budget base case (EV_BUDGET27_CAPEX_RAILWAY's own assumption), and growth is decelerating. The fiscal deficit at 42.1% of BE in H1 is a five-year high, and the ET report of 2 Oct 2026 expects capex to moderate in H2. Monthly CGA releases were public all along, so this is not unpriced news. The surprise since June is ~+2pp of growth, giving 0.2-0.3 SSU. At 1.0 the node is the largest positive since-June driver for TMCV (+4.0), CUMMINSIND/SIEMENS (+2.5), AMBUJACEM (+2.2), PNB/UNIONBANK (+2.0), ABB (+1.5) and IRFC (+1.2), and it feeds directly into 'unpriced' upside for ABB, SIEMENS, CUMMINSIND, AMBUJACEM and IRFC.

This is a CUMMINSIND-only node. Q2 FY27 results (4 Nov 2026) showed revenue +4%, EBITDA margin down 680 bp y/y (~22% to ~15%) and PAT down 19-27%. The shares fell 14-15% on 5 Nov (ET, CNBC-TV18, Business Standard, NDTV Profit). EBITDA fell ~29% y/y, about twice the node's 1-SSU definition (-15% EBITDA). Without this state the model reports +6.25% 'unpriced' upside against a -31% realised move whose main cause is a stock-specific results miss, which the brief says must not be called unpriced. A state of 1.0 is conservative given that the call commentary (cause: price, mix or cost) is pending.

findings.subject: BRITANNIA
findings.issue: VERDICT: agree — rank 106 (12m -0.35%). The Q2 FY27 results event is dated 2026-11-06 but results are scheduled for 5 Nov (Upstox list, 5 Nov). Its negative skew ([-8, 6], expected -0.9) repeats the sugar and palm cost pressure that the graph already books through F_SUGAR (observed +2.78 SSU, -2.2). Fix: {ticker: BRITANNIA, match: 'Q2 FY27 results', date: '2026-11-05', impact_pct_low: -7.0, impact_pct_high: 7.0}. Also drop F_GOLD (edge_scale). The net change is about +0.5pp. It is defensive (beta 0.73) with no missing large channel.

findings.subject: GAIL
findings.issue: VERDICT: agree — rank 57 (12m +1.8%). Unpriced is 0 (realised +7.9% exceeds the model's +3.6%), and forward +4.4 comes mostly from the beta adjustment: raw forward exposure is +0.2, and beta 1.28 times the universe mean of -3.3 adds about +4.2. The C_MIDEAST_CONFLICT edge duplicates F_GAS_GLOBAL (edge_scale 0.33). The F_GAS_GLOBAL sign is debatable: GAIL's ~5.8 mtpa of Henry-Hub-linked US LNG gains when JKM spikes (2022 precedent, model knowledge). This is not a flip, but the -1.5 central value could be -0.5. Company events are reasonable: the GAIL Gas IPO board approval of 30 Oct and the PNGRB tariff risk.

findings.subject: TVSMOTOR
findings.issue: VERDICT: agree — rank 79 (12m +0.7%). The realised +27% market-adjusted is far above the model's +0.7, and unpriced is correctly 0. The since-June P_EV_POLICY +1.1 x 3.0 = +3.3 includes CAFE-III (+0.8), which applies to passenger cars, not two-wheelers. The PM E-DRIVE extension came with an e2W incentive cut, so the net for TVS is about 0. This has no ranking effect today but is a node-conflation risk for forward EV events (split P_EV_POLICY by segment). Company events check: the consumer-finance demerger was approved by the board on 28 Oct (TOI, BusinessLine, Business Standard). p 0.35 for completion by Jul 2027 at [-2, 5] is reasonable. F_US_10Y is halved (edge_scale).

findings.subject: Methodology note: 'unpriced' for de-rated high-multiple names
findings.issue: For ABB, SIEMENS, CUMMINSIND, TATAPOWER, ADANIGREEN, ADANIENSOL, AMBUJACEM and IRFC, the realised under-performance coincides with dated stock- or sector-specific news: results misses, the 20-23 Oct capital-goods de-rating, OFS supply, arbitration losses, and Adani/Tata group flows. The graph has no node for these, so the unpriced term reads them as a mean-reversion opportunity even though the bound prevents overshoot. Suggestion: when a profile's current_state lists a dated results miss or de-rating inside the window, cap RECENT_CONVERGENCE for that company at 0.25 (12m) or zero it. Otherwise this residual is the main reason 8 of my 18 names sit in the top 60.
